lesson.title: Security of processing
lesson.summary: Choose security measures appropriate to the risk, and test that they work.

prerequisites.reason: Pseudonymisation is one of the listed security measures.
Article 32 implements the integrity and confidentiality principle.

blocks: Article 32(1): taking into account the state of the art, the costs, the nature, scope, context and purposes of processing, and the risks, the **controller and the processor** must implement measures to ensure a level of security **appropriate to the risk**.
So security is neither "maximum regardless of cost" nor "cheapest possible". It is matched to the risk.
Article 32(1) lists measures to use as appropriate:

items: (b) ensuring ongoing **confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience** of systems;
(c) the ability to **restore** availability and access in a timely manner after an incident;
(d) a process for **regularly testing, assessing and evaluating** the measures.

blocks: When assessing the risk, consider in particular accidental or unlawful **destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to** personal data (Article 32(2)).
Organisations must take steps so that anyone acting under their authority with access to personal data processes it **only on instructions** (Article 32(4)).
Following an approved code of conduct or certification can help demonstrate compliance (Article 32(3)).
Sunfield's measures, scaled to its risks:

items: access to staff files only for the manager and payroll;
daily backups of the order system, with a restore that is actually tested;
a yearly review of whether the measures still work.

blocks: Buying a firewall once and never checking it does not meet point (d).

blocks.text: These Sunfield examples are **illustrations**. A real assessment depends on all the facts.
